title: Acceptance criteria: deterministic response envelopes, tool handshake timeouts, and progressive schema recovery
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket captures product-level acceptance criteria for a predictable, debuggable contract between Redwood APIs and downstream tool integrations when models emit machine-readable output. Focus areas: 1) deterministic response envelopes that make it straightforward for clients to reconcile partial streams and final objects; 2) explicit handshake and timeout semantics for tool/function invocation during streaming and non-streaming flows; 3) recovery and reconciliation rules for malformed/truncated structured payloads emitted mid-stream. The goal is to unblock API, SDK, runtime, and QA teams with a clear pass/fail checklist and representative test vectors.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope baseline: every structured response (streamed or non-streamed) MUST include a top-level 'rwd_meta' envelope when structural output is requested. The envelope contains: schema_version (semver string), message_id (UUID), chunk_sequence (int for streamed chunks), chunk_checksum (hex), and final_flag (boolean).

Atomic function-call compatibility: function/tool calls invoked in non-streamed mode MUST follow existing function_call semantics (name + arguments). When function calls occur inside a stream, each emitted function-call chunk MUST be accompanied by a chunk_sequence and partial_arguments marker to support incremental argument assembly on the client side.

Progressive schema recovery: SDKs must reconstruct a valid JSON object after a partial stream if the final chunk is missing due to connection tear. Acceptance requires a deterministic rehydration algorithm in the SDK using chunk_sequence ordering and checksums to identify missing chunks and raise a specific error type 'rwd_stream_incomplete' with a recommended retry window and idempotency token.

Error classification and handling guidance: define three error classes: recoverable (transient network or missing chunk -> client retries), resolvable (schema mismatch -> client initiates schema negotiation or fallback model), and fatal (malformed JSON with inconsistent checksums -> abort and surface server error). For each class, an example payload and the expected API/SDK behavior must be provided.

Backpressure and timeouts for tool handshakes: tool providers must receive a handshake request within T_handshake (configurable; default 3s). If a tool doesn't acknowledge within T_handshake, Redwood runtime will emit a structured fallback (rwd_meta.fallback_reason set) and continue generation with a pre-designated fallback policy. Tests must cover immediate handshake, delayed ack within T_handshake, and timeouts beyond T_handshake.

Idempotent retries: repeated retries of a function/tool call MUST include the same idempotency token from the original message_id. Acceptance requires a test demonstrating that duplicate handshakes do not trigger duplicate side-effects against a mock tool backend.

Streaming termination semantics: streamed structured responses must expose a deterministic finalization event. Clients must be able to detect 'final_flag=true' in the rwd_meta of the last chunk and validate final assembly via a final checksum. Acceptance requires end-to-end test where 500 concurrent streaming responses finalize correctly within latency SLOs.

Compatibility with existing SDKs: when structured output is not requested, existing chat/text behavior must not change. Acceptance requires regression test suite run against the current SDKs demonstrating zero changes in non-structured endpoints.

Observability hooks: every structured stream must emit traceable events to the Console with event names: stream.start, tool.handshake, stream.chunk, stream.finalize, stream.error. The acceptance test will assert presence of these events for a representative run in staging.

Documentation and sample code: update SDK docs with a minimal example showing: 1) receiving chunked structured output, 2) reconstructing partial arguments for a function call, 3) handling rwd_stream_incomplete and recommended retry flow. Acceptance requires a short runnable sample in the repo referenced in 'references'.
test_cases: Happy path: non-streamed structured object returned with rwd_meta, single checksum matches, no tool calls.
Streamed function-call: sequence of three chunks produce a single valid function invocation; client reassembles and invokes mock tool exactly once.
Missing chunk: simulate a dropped middle chunk; SDK identifies missing chunk_sequence, raises rwd_stream_incomplete, and exposes missing sequence numbers in the error metadata.
Checksum mismatch: corrupt chunk content -> SDK marks chunk as invalid and classifies as fatal; runtime surfaces server error and increments metric stream.checksum_failures.
Handshake timeout: mock tool does not ack within T_handshake -> runtime emits fallback stream chunk and tags event tool.handshake_timeout.
Backwards compatibility: call non-structured endpoint and assert identical payload shape as pre-change baseline.
decisions: Adopt a lightweight rwd_meta envelope instead of embedding schema fields at arbitrary positions in the payload to simplify SDK parsing across languages.
Default handshake timeout T_handshake=3s, configurable per-customer via Dedicated/Private deployments.
Require final_flag and chunk_checksum for all streams where structured=True; streaming free-form text remains unchanged.
Idempotency token is the message_id generated by Redwood; clients may override but must include original to avoid duplicate side-effects.
